description: Re-anchor supervisor auto-ship on the terminal complete+CLEAN state (not the transient review->CLEAN edge) with a persisted fire-once marker, fixing the bypassed await-operator gate and the re-entry reachability miss.

userStories.title: Re-anchor auto-ship to terminal complete+CLEAN with a persisted fire-once marker
userStories.description: As the cam supervisor, I need the auto-ship dispatch to fire from the terminal 'complete' state gated on review.lastVerdict==='CLEAN' with a persisted review.autoShipDispatchedAt marker, so that a pending requires:'operator' story correctly gates the ship (await-operator) and a re-entry / sidecar restart re-dispatches auto-ship exactly once.
acceptanceCriteria: opts.autoShipFn() no longer lives in the review branch (action.kind==='review'); it is invoked only from the terminal 'complete' branch, gated on prd.review.lastVerdict==='CLEAN'. The previous review-branch callsite (loop.ts ~1350-1356) is removed. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/auto-chain.test.ts]
A PRD with a pending requires:'operator' story and review CLEAN routes to await-operator and autoShipFn is NOT called (BUG A path, new test). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/auto-chain.test.ts]
Re-entry with review.lastVerdict==='CLEAN' already persisted and all stories passing dispatches auto-ship exactly once (BUG B path, new test). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/auto-chain.test.ts]

Two runSupervisor invocations over the same complete+CLEAN prd call autoShipFn once in total; the review.autoShipDispatchedAt marker guards the re-dispatch (cross-invocation test with shared mutable prd). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/auto-chain.test.ts]
Terminal 'complete' reached via MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT (not CLEAN) does NOT dispatch auto-ship (new test). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/auto-chain.test.ts]

review.autoShipDispatchedAt is written to prd.json via writePrd BEFORE autoShipFn is called, and the marker field is added to the PrdSnapshot review type. [oracle: grep -q 'autoShipDispatchedAt' src/supervisor/decide.ts && grep -q 'autoShipDispatchedAt' src/supervisor/loop.ts]

ship-finalize removes scripts/cam/prd.json (git rm), so a fresh cycle re-arms the marker; scripts/cam/prd.json remains in the finalize harnessPaths list. [oracle: grep -q 'scripts/cam/prd.json' src/commands/ship-finalize.ts]

No redundant operator check is added at the auto-ship callsite (complete is unreachable while a requires:'operator' story is pending; the gate is already covered by decide.ts). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine passes: bun run check:all exits 0 (typecheck + biome + tests). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Core change in src/supervisor/loop.ts. (1) In the terminal 'complete' branch (loop.ts:718-738), after the existing promoteVerdictTo handling, add: if opts.autoShipFn !== undefined && prd.review?.lastVerdict === 'CLEAN' && prd.review?.autoShipDispatchedAt === undefined, then writePrd({ ...prd, review: { ...prd.review, autoShipDispatchedAt: clock() } }) and call opts.autoShipFn(). Write the marker BEFORE the dispatch. (2) Delete the old callsite in the review branch (loop.ts:1350-1356). (3) Add autoShipDispatchedAt?: string to the review shape of PrdSnapshot in src/supervisor/decide.ts (lines 30-35). GOTCHA (from issue): 'complete' is ALSO reached with lastVerdict==='MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT' (debt terminal + promoteVerdictTo) -- gate strictly on ==='CLEAN' so debt escalates rather than ships. GOTCHA: the intra-invocation dedup is moot (complete returns immediately); the real risk is cross-invocation / sidecar restart (in-place binary swap), hence the PERSISTED marker, NOT the in-memory blockedCycleEmitted flag (CAM-139 US-005 pattern in sidecar.ts). GOTCHA: the supervisor already owns prd.review writes (verdicts), so adding autoShipDispatchedAt there is consistent; the 'orchestrator does not modify prd.json' rule does not apply to the supervisor. Tests: extend test/supervisor/auto-chain.test.ts -- the existing makePrd helper hardcodes requires:null; add a variant with a requires:'operator' pending story (path A), a re-entry prd pre-seeded with lastVerdict CLEAN + no marker (path B), a shared-mutable-prd cross-invocation case for dedup, and a MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT complete case. Read scripts/cam/patterns.md at story start. noUncheckedIndexedAccess is on: guard array/optional access.

userStories.title: Record ADR 0008 for the auto-ship terminal anchoring and persisted dedup
userStories.description: As a future maintainer, I need an ADR that documents the terminal 'complete' anchoring of auto-ship, the persisted fire-once marker, and the principled divergence from in-memory dedup, so the surprising persisted-vs-in-memory choice is legible without re-deriving it from the code.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/adr/0008-<slug>.md exists and follows the repo ADR format (Status, Data, Contexto, Decisao sections) as in docs/adr/0007-inter-cycle-unattended-drain.md. [oracle: ls docs/adr/0008-*.md]

The ADR documents that auto-ship is anchored on the terminal 'complete' state gated on review.lastVerdict==='CLEAN' (not the transient review->CLEAN edge), and that this makes the await-operator gate fall out for free. [oracle: grep -qi 'complete' docs/adr/0008-*.md]

The ADR documents the persisted review.autoShipDispatchedAt fire-once marker and why it is persisted (survives sidecar restart / in-place binary swap) rather than an in-memory flag. [oracle: grep -q 'autoShipDispatchedAt' docs/adr/0008-*.md]

The ADR documents the principled divergence from the in-memory dedup precedent (CAM-139 US-005 blockedCycleEmitted; the CAM-181 spec AC labels this precedent CAM-68 -- reconcile the reference to the actual in-memory dedup site). [oracle: grep -qi 'in-memory' docs/adr/0008-*.md]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine passes: bun run check:all exits 0. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New file docs/adr/0008-auto-ship-terminal-anchor.md. Mirror the format of docs/adr/0007-inter-cycle-unattended-drain.md (headers in Portuguese, no travessao/emoji per the repo doc convention). This decision passes all three ADR gates: hard to reverse (moving the dispatch anchor + adding a persisted prd field), surprising without context (why a persisted marker instead of the in-memory blockedCycleEmitted flag used in CAM-139 US-005), and a genuine trade-off (persisted marker survives restart but adds a prd.json field the supervisor must manage). DISCREPANCY to reconcile: the CAM-181 spec's ADR acceptance criterion cites 'CAM-68 (dedup in-memory)', but CAM-68 is about gitignoring runtime markers; the actual in-memory dedup precedent is CAM-139 US-005's blockedCycleEmitted (src/commands/sidecar.ts:820,891). Document the divergence against the real in-memory dedup site. Depends on US-001 (documents the behavior US-001 implements).
